title: I created an asset generator after 11 months of work that produces thousands of animated game assets in seconds — completely offline, with no AI required!
author: Buchedegato
selftext:
¡Olis!   
I'm finally launching my project after almost 11 months of work! I hope you enjoy it and that it proves useful to many developers. It's an asset generator that works without AI and without an internet connection, if you prefer. It runs on both Windows and Linux.

The idea is very simple: you want an asset, you type it in, and the program generates it for you, complete with multiple animations, perfectly sequenced and logically consistent, ranging from combat animations to everyday activities.

It handles thousands of concepts at an almost absurd level of detail. You can request a hoplite soldier from any Greek city-state and it will generate one; a soldier from any Chinese dynasty, Hittites, Assyrians, Macedonians, all kinds of medieval troops (including military orders), Roman soldiers from every historical period, Celts, Gauls, Goths, Alans, African tribes, Amazons... You can request an Aztec, Olmec, or Inca warrior, even from much older cultures such as the Teotihuacans, and it will generate them in seconds, with historical accuracy. Currently, it covers everything from the Stone Age to the pre-industrial era, so you can create troops from the Napoleonic Wars, the revolutions in the Americas, the Zulu Wars, and much, much more.

Everything it generates already comes with a wide variety of animations: attacking, defending, running, walking, reloading, dying, throwing bombs or torches, mining, digging, talking, eating, fishing, and much more.

If, for any reason, there's something it can't generate, or an animation you'd like to have, you can simply ask any AI to create a JSON file describing what you want, paste it into the program, and it will generate your custom animation or design.

But that's not all! You can create over 200 different tree species and more than 500 types of flowers, plants, grass, and rocks, all with plenty of variety. You won't always get the same tree, even if you make exactly the same request. The same goes for flowers and units: you can request an Aztec soldier, and the next one you generate will always look different. You can also customize their equipment, colors, ethnicity, and much more.

And it doesn't stop there. All trees, plants, and flowers come with multiple customization options. For each one, you can choose any of the four seasons, and the asset will adapt accordingly, including the correct seasonal fruits. You can also enable wind, falling leaves, or fallen fruit on the ground. Plants have the same options, and for those developing gathering or harvesting games, there are even versions where the flower has already been picked. This applies to absolutely every model. There's also an option to make objects appear at their real-world scale relative to soldiers.

But there's even more! There are over 90 animal species, along with their juvenile versions, all featuring unique animations. Dolphins jump and splash, horses gallop, crocodiles perform their famous death roll, and turtles lay eggs. On top of that, you can enable mounted units riding horses, camels, or elephants, each with their own movement and attack animations.

And we're still not done! There are hundreds of objects to decorate your world, from chairs, tables, and chandeliers to forges and alchemy tables, all with animations and endless variations. Want a Roman-style alchemy table? Here it is. Prefer a Chinese-style food stall? You've got it. An Aztec-style one? Absolutely! And these aren't just simple color or texture changes: each object is adapted to its respective culture. For example, Aztec food stalls are set up on the ground over blankets, while Chinese candles are placed inside bamboo stumps. Every object is generated differently from the previous one. You can customize its colors and materials, and many objects include animations.

But I'm not stopping there. You can create buildings and monuments and give them their own personality by customizing floors, width, and decorations. And if you don't want to use a pre-designed building, you can build one yourself! There are hundreds of modular pieces for walls, floors, roofs, and windows, all customizable to create different window designs, materials, and doors (open, glazed, and positioned at whatever height you want).

And there's still more. You can generate dozens of visual effects: explosions, magic, level-ups, foraging effects, tree-felling, mining, sword movements, and weather effects such as snow and rain. You can scale them up or down, increase the number of particles, and change their colors. You can add bees, fireflies, or flies, choosing exactly how many you want and how widely dispersed they should be, all with their own animations. It even includes clouds!

But wait, there's more. Siege weapons: over 30 types with more than 500 different models, including some particularly unusual ones such as Greek fire, springalds, and battering rams. You can choose whether they come with a crew or without one, complete with their respective animations. And if, for any reason, you don't want projectiles to appear when using ranged weapons, you can disable them. This also applies to archers, crossbowmen, slingers, and soldiers equipped with blowguns or javelins.

Still not enough? How about terrain? You can create hundreds of different terrain types: grass, ice, snow, lava, and water (with adjustable transparency). You can also create over 30 types of paths and bridges using any terrain you want, customize their elevation, add cliffs and even waterfalls, all with animations, seasonal variations, and customizable colors.

And I'm not done yet! Want to create a farming game? You have over 50 different crop plots. Just like terrain, you can make them as small or as large as you want, with wind animations and harvesting options, all adapted to the seasons. A wheat field won't look the same in spring as it does in autumn, when it's ready for harvest.

Need even more assets to get started? I've included over 400 icon families with more than 5,000 variations, which can also be animated if you wish. As an extra, there are fantasy units such as ogres, gargoyles, and skeletons.

But perhaps you'll tell me you don't like the art style. No worries! The program currently supports three art styles: voxel, chibi, and pixel art. Like the Hungarian soldier you just created but want it in pixel art? No problem! Simply switch from voxel to pixel art, and you'll have it ready with all its animations. This applies to absolutely everything you generate.

There are 19 color palettes, ranging from dark and vibrant palettes to 16-bit and 8-bit styles. You can choose unit outlines and line smoothing. You can remove blood or give your units team colors if you want to create your own Age of Empires-style game. You can also switch to a side view (2D) or an overhead view, with 8 directional facings.

Just by combining the available style options, each sprite has 1,400,832 possible appearances, bringing the total to nearly 98 quintillion possible combinations!

Coming soon, I'll be adding more styles, such as hand-drawn and NES, and I'll also be working on an art style similar to Age of Empires, American Conquest, and Cossacks.

And there's still more! The program is available in 28 languages. In future updates, I'll be adding more historical periods and fantasy units, as well as more animals, trees, and objects, along with the ability to generate user interfaces (UI). Later on, I'll also add the ability to generate ships.

You can choose the format in which you want to export your creations: PNG, BMP, TGA, animated GIF, JSON atlas, and compatibility with Godot and Unity.

This is an 11-month project. I received a lot of help from DeepSeek with the interface and translations, while the free version of Claude helped me identify bugs during the final stages of this release.

I hope you enjoy it and find it useful, especially developers who struggle to get consistent assets with proper animations. It doesn't use tokens or AI: you can run it on a computer without an internet connection. I've included a free demo on the website where you can try out everything it can do.

It will be discounted during its first week, and all future updates will be completely free. If there's enough demand, I'll also release a Mac version.

Everything you create can be used in your commercial games, with no credit required.

🔗 **Demo and download:** [https://buchedegato.itch.io/my-magic-asset-workshop](https://buchedegato.itch.io/my-magic-asset-workshop)

💬 **Discord:** [https://discord.gg/DBmXaSBck](https://discord.gg/DBmXaSBck)

replies.author: Buchedegato

Thank you very much for trying it and for the detailed feedback, this really helps! You're right, English support still has some glitches. I will add more English words and classic fantasy classes (thief, rogue, paladin, wizard...) in the next updates. I'll let you know when it comes out! 🐾

replies.author: Buchedegato
replies.body:
It’s procedural generation, kind of like how Minecraft builds its worlds, but for sprites. I spent months writing the rules by hand: body shapes, armour and weapons for each culture, colors, animations, etc. When you type “hoplite” it looks up that word, picks the helmet, shield and spear that go with it, and a random seed changes the small details so each one comes out a bit different.

Easiest way to check is the free demo. It works with no internet at all, and if you use the same seed you get the exact same sprite every time. If you type something it doesn’t know, it just tells you it doesn’t recognize it instead of making something up.

Some words may fail, several languages are in beta, as the number of words is millions, but I am working hard to make this work well.

replies.author: Buchedegato
replies.body:
Not pre-made! Nothing is stored as finished art. Every asset is built on the spot from code: simple 3D shapes (boxes, spheres, cylinders) assembled by rules for each culture, plant or building, with a skeleton for the animations. The seed decides the details, so you can keep rolling new variants.

And yes, it’s 3D voxel models rendered as 2D sprites from whatever view you pick (isometric, side or top-down) in 8 directions. Pixel art and chibi are different ways of rendering the same model.

The original project file weighs only 5mb, when converted to exe, it went up to 100 I don't know why, but there is no physical asset really existing.

comments.author: Professional_Gur6945
comments.body: What is the underlying tech stack for this?

replies.author: Buchedegato
replies.body: It’s all plain JavaScript in a single HTML file, no frameworks or game engine. It has its own small voxel renderer drawing on a 2D canvas, and the GIF, ZIP and sprite sheet export are written from scratch too. The desktop version is just that file wrapped in Electron (AppImage for Linux, .exe for Windows). That’s why it runs fully offline.
